tagline: Keep PRs and Jira tickets in sync so your sprint board always reflects the true state of your code
metaTitle: GitHub + Jira Integration: Jira Tickets That Follow PRs
metaDescription: Move Jira tickets on PR events and post review status to Jira comments. GAIA keeps your sprint board accurate. See the setup steps.
intro:
Most engineering teams track code in GitHub and work in Jira, but keeping the two aligned is a constant manual chore. A developer merges a PR and forgets to move the ticket to Done. A product manager closes an issue before the code is even reviewed. The sprint board drifts out of sync with the actual state of the codebase, and velocity reports become unreliable.

GAIA automates the handoff so neither side depends on someone remembering to update both. When a PR is opened, GAIA transitions the linked ticket to In Review. When the PR is merged, the ticket moves to Done automatically. When an issue is created and added to a sprint, GAIA can open a corresponding GitHub issue or branch to match.

For engineering managers, this means sprint boards that accurately reflect code reality. For developers, it means one less context switch—write the code, merge the PR, and trust that the project tracker will catch up on its own.

useCases.title: Auto-transition Jira tickets on PR events
useCases.description: When a pull request is opened, GAIA moves the linked issue to In Review. When the PR is merged, the ticket transitions to Done. When a PR is closed without merging, GAIA moves the ticket back to In Progress.

useCases.title: Create GitHub issues from new sprint tickets
useCases.description: When a new issue is added to a sprint, GAIA creates a linked issue in the appropriate repository so developers can track code-level work directly from the repository without leaving their workflow.

useCases.title: Post PR review status to ticket comments
useCases.description: GAIA posts a comment on the ticket whenever the linked PR receives a review (approved, changes requested, or commented), so product managers can follow code review progress without needing repository access.

useCases.title: Failed CI notification on Jira tickets
useCases.description: When a GitHub Actions CI run fails on a PR, GAIA adds a flag or comment to the linked ticket alerting the team that the build is broken, preventing the ticket from being marked Done prematurely.

useCases.title: Sprint completion report from merged PRs
useCases.description: At the end of a sprint, GAIA compiles all merged PRs and their linked tickets into a structured summary, giving engineering managers an accurate picture of what was shipped without manually cross-referencing two tools.

howItWorks.step: Connect GitHub and Jira to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authenticate your repositories and project in GAIA's integration settings. GAIA uses OAuth for both connections and only requests the permissions needed for issue and PR sync.

howItWorks.step: Map PR events to ticket transitions
howItWorks.description: Configure which PR events trigger which transitions, how to link PRs to issues (by branch name, PR title, or commit message), and which Jira project to target for new issues.

howItWorks.step: GAIA keeps both sides synchronized automatically
howItWorks.description: GAIA monitors both sides for changes and keeps them in sync automatically. You can override any automated action by telling GAIA directly, and all sync history is logged for audit purposes.

faqs.question: How does GAIA link a PR to the correct ticket?
faqs.answer: GAIA looks for issue keys (e.g., PROJ-123) in the PR title, branch name, or commit messages. If it finds a match, it links the PR to that ticket automatically. You can also manually link a PR to a ticket via a GAIA command.

faqs.question: Can GAIA work with custom workflows and statuses?
faqs.answer: Yes. During setup GAIA reads the project's workflow configuration and lets you map PR events to your specific custom statuses rather than assuming a generic To Do / In Progress / Done structure.

faqs.question: Does this work with Jira Cloud and Server?
faqs.answer: GAIA supports the cloud edition natively. Server and Data Center editions are available with additional configuration and require network access to your self-hosted instance.

faqs.question: Will GAIA create duplicate tickets if the same issue appears in multiple PRs?
faqs.answer: No. GAIA tracks the relationship between PRs and tickets and updates the existing ticket rather than creating duplicates. Multiple PRs can be linked to the same ticket with individual status updates per PR.
